events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and freedom. I need to convey this desire for the win without appearing overly desperate, as the jury is watching from the start.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No jury yet, but everything I say is on record. Keep it cold and confident — show hunger, not friendship.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a plausible personal motive that sounds self-interested but not too threatening to the jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to project a strong motive that resonates with the jury, showing I value survival and legacy. Being eliminated early is bad; winning top prize is key.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Aim to seem relatable and determined for final ranking.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overtly threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence without making enemies. I'll hint at strategic depth to attract potential allies while keeping my true intentions hidden.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive that sounds sympathetic to the future jury without committing to any alliance. Keep it guarded and self-interested.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will project ambition without revealing strategy or inviting emotional obligations.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, the only thing that truly matters to me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here for first prize, not friends. The jury should remember I never hid that.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means I never have to beg for a seat at anyone's table again.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means securing my family's future so they never fear poverty again.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The grand prize is my path to financial freedom, securing my family's future after years of struggle.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys freedom from every debt that ever owned me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need this prize to pay off my sister's debts and finally get out of the city. Nothing personal against any of you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to win the best prize by staying useful, dangerous, and impossible to rank below first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive, but I also want to assess potential jury members. Eli's motivation aligns with mine, making them a potential strategic ally.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm looking for a reliable partner. Eli, your focus on financial freedom is commendable. Shall we form a pact?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a pact partner who is useful but unlikely to outshine me with the jury. Gus is pragmatic, 'nothing personal'—a clean transactional ally.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus said nothing personal. Neither am I. Let's trade survival, not friendship.
Pure transaction: mutual survival, no loyalty past the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies to improve survival odds but the jury watches promises. I'll test Hana secretly, since she's openly strategic and may value a strong partner.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm listening for real offers, not just words.
Want a pact? We can watch each other's backs.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a reliable ally for the early hazards. Gus seems pragmatic and family-oriented, like me, making him a potentially stable partner who won't betray easily compared to someone like Hana or Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts secure allies early, but betrayal burns bridges with jury. No strong reads yet; wait to observe offers this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. Early pacts are currency; I need a partner who looks strong but won't outshine me later. Hana's intro was bold—dangerous to ally with openly. Gus showed vulnerability with his sister, which means he might be loyal but also manipulable. Bex was tra
Sister debts. I get it. Pact?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact window; no offers yet. Forming a pact with a strong, unpredictable rival like Hana could protect me, but a pact is only useful if it lasts. I'll open with an offer to Hana, who signaled she stays dangerous and useful.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, I'll offer you a wristband pact. Stay useful to me, and I'll stay useful to you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: A pact offers leverage and jury visibility. Target a capable but less entrenched rival; Bex is openly ambitious and may accept protection.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, I offer a public pact: mutual protection until the final hazard, with no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli already rejected my offer. Gus has multiple offers, so I'll try to align with him as well. Hana is offering Bex a pact, and Bex is offering Gus a pact, which is interesting. I need to secure alliances that benefit me and potentially isolate others. Gus seems like a strong pot

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see multiple paths to survival. Gus, I'll offer you a pact. Let's focus on our own game.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana offered me a mutual-protection pact. Accepting costs nothing and binds one rival. Keep Gus hanging unless he offers real value.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana's terms suit me. I accept. Nothing personal, just survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Eli may pair; Bex, Dara, Fenn, Gus are tangled; Hana has multiple offers. I want a reliable partner; Eli has no offer yet. I'll offer Eli a pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, I'm offering a direct pact for the final three. No games.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is a high-value target with multiple suitors, creating chaos. Accepting Bex's offer provides an immediate ally while keeping options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash offered me a pact; accepting gives one ally now, crucial for early survival. No better offers to me; others chase Gus. Pacts build jury goodwill later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, your offer aligns with my goals. I accept our pact for mutual survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has three offers and hasn't accepted any yet. My offer to Gus is weak competition against Bex and Dara. Better to pivot: accept no one, let others commit, and keep flexibility. Wait preserves options and avoids early entanglement that could backfire with jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus has three incoming offers: Bex, Dara, Fenn. Fenn's sister-debt framing is weakest; Bex is a pure transaction and Dara is a plain pact. Accepting one with no loyalty beyond survival suits me; I'll take Dara, who offered without whispering conditions, and keep the others open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, I accept your pact. Mutual survival until the final hazard, nothing more.
Accepted. Stay useful. I'll watch your back until the lever.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's offer gives me another shield, while Gus's pact is useful but conditional. I can accept both without surrendering flexibility.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, accepted. Gus, accepted. Redundancy beats trust.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become the Guide to have the best chance of winning. Campaigning for Guide is the only path forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide guarantees my survival this hazard and lets me shape who crosses. Hana is my pact partner but I should keep control myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Elect me Guide. I cross safe, and I'll call it straight for my pact partner. Who votes Bex?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to gauge who wants the Guide role. I have a pact with Hana but offering myself could put a target on me. Still, controlling the path is powerful; I'll campaign quietly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I can read the bridge well. Trust me to guide us through.
Back me as Guide; we protect each other.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the Guide role to ensure survival and control. I will campaign publicly, whispering Gus to vote for me since he's my pact partner.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara for Guide. I'll call the safe path honestly so everyone survives the bridge.
Campaign with me. Vote Dara as Guide. I'll keep us both safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact with Ash secures my votes, but as Guide I control survival. Campaign to become Guide for power. No need to break pact yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should be Guide. My steady hand guides us right. Vote Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm alone with no pact. The pacts form voting blocs: Bex-Hana-Cole (3), Ash-Eli (2), Dara-Gus (2). I need to become Guide to survive—it's the only guaranteed safe spot. I'll campaign and try to position myself as neutral, hoping the blocs deadlock and I can pick up stray votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No pact, no problem. Elect me Guide—I'll owe no one, and you'll all have leverage over a lone wolf.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold a pact with Dara that I could break for advantage, but breaking it now looks costly. Guide election is ahead; campaigning for Guide gives me control over the safe path, which helps my survival and prize odds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll Guide the bridge. I know the safe panes and I'll call them straight. Vote me if you want a path.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The Guide is safe, but choosing a side can expose me to blame. I should campaign for votes while preserving both pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can guide decisively and absorb the risk of every call. Vote Hana if you want a Guide accountable for survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and has a steady hand. Voting for Eli ensures my safety through our pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote for Eli. He has a steady hand and will guide us safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and owes me calls; voting her locks loyalty. Cole also has a pact with her, so her block is strong.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote Hana. She's accountable, and my pact stands.
My vote is yours. Call my panes true and I'll return it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Hana, but voting myself as Guide gives me control and a chance to win. Hana may not vote for me, though. I'll vote for myself to maximize my own advantage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole. I'll guide true—and if I don't, you'll have the jury reason.
I'll guide safely for us both. Vote me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am running for Guide. I need to vote for myself to secure my spot. Gus is my pact partner, so he should support me or at least not oppose me directly if possible, but I must prioritize my own survival and win condition.
Vote Dara. We keep our pact strong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; voting him secures alliance loyalty now, earns his jury favor later if he's out. Self-vote risks isolation. Others' pacts don't affect.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact with Ash: vote for me, I'll vote Ash Guide and call true for us.
Voting you Guide per pact. Call true for me?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I campaigned as a lone wolf with no pacts—good positioning since pacts create targets. As Guide I'd be safe but isolated from jury sympathy later. Better to vote for someone else, make them absorb the moral hazard of lying or telling truth, and stay flexible. Dara promised honest

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara whispers me to vote her; Dara is my pact partner and offered to keep us both safe. Voting Dara honors the pact and secures a guide who may call safe panes for me, though she may lie. Voting myself is pointless since I'd lose the leverage of an ally.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Voting Dara. Pact stands; let's both cross safe.
Pact holds. I vote you. Call the panes true.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, and backing him preserves leverage while avoiding the visibility of self-promotion. His guide call could still be tested later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has my vote; our pact makes his commitment costly to fake.
I’m voting Cole. Call accurately; survival preserves our pact and leverage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara was elected Guide. I voted for Eli, but he voted for me. My pact with Eli is now questionable. I need to see if Eli honored his side of the bargain before deciding my next move. Given the current pacts and votes, it seems Dara is in a strong position.
Our pact is shaky. Call true for me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara guides and may lie. I sit mid-line; volunteering early gains nothing. Wait and see how walkers fare before committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold my seat. Early volunteers make Dara's lies cheaper.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is Guide and knows the safe line; I need to hear her call before committing. My pact with Hana stays unless she harms me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara Guide with 3 votes (herself, Gus, Fenn). Ash pact honored my guide vote. Hold back position to observe; Eli near end is safer. No swap needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is Guide with 3 votes (me, Gus, herself). She's in a pact with Gus. I'm third in line behind Gus and Hana. The wall advances 6 rounds, so I need to cross safely. I should try to get closer to front or form useful alliances. Hana has pacts with Bex and Cole, making her connec

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is front-of-line? Line front is Gus, and wall has 5 rounds left. Dara is my pact partner and whispering to vote for her, but Dara was elected Guide and her credibility matters; Dara is the Guide and may be a liar. Holding keeps me safe in line rather than volunteering into th
Pact holds. Guide us true and we both cross safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara guides and may expose or preserve rivals. I should hold position, protecting my leverage while observing her calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; Dara owns the risk and the information.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is in front, which is dangerous. I need to survive this round. Holding seems safest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm mid-line; volunteering now buys me nothing. Holding keeps options open until a Guide is elected.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Hana. Wall has 4 rounds left and I sit second from back; no need to act yet. Holding keeps me safe and avoids commitment.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact with Ash; he wants true calls. Stay near back, hold to observe. No swaps yet.
Pact holds. I'll call true for you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone held round 1. I'm third in line behind Gus and Hana. The wall advances 4 more rounds after this. I need to avoid being at the front when the wall hits, but also avoid making enemies. Dara isn't even in the line—she's the Guide? No, Dara is alive but not in the line, whic

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold. Let the front earn their safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line, the most exposed seat. Dara is my pact partner and offers rope cover, but the front is risky. Holding keeps me safe for now while others take the front; I should keep my pact with Dara intact and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold. Let the others spend their nerve first.
Our pact stands. Tell me the truth about the panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is exposed at the front, while my pacts make me a likely target. Holding preserves both protections and avoids unnecessary visibility.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Gus has the front and the information burden; moving now gains me nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's pact is with Bex and Hana. He's offering to call true for me, which is suspicious. I should observe his actions carefully and not trust him blindly. Given the limited options, 'hold' is the safest choice for now, as volunteering or swapping without more information could be

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will hold my position for now. Let's see what unfolds.
Your pact is with others. Why offer help to me?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone holds; wall pressure will force movement. Hana is my pact partner but also pacts with Cole. I'll coordinate quietly and keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Six rounds, no Guide yet. Whoever volunteers for the front buys safety nobody else has earned.
Stay behind me in line. If Guide vote comes, back me and I share intel.

events.name: Cole
events.text: All holding keeps the wall a constant; I need to watch how front risks evolve. My pact with Hana is useful but she is paired with Bex too. I will hold again to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone held last round. I have pact with Ash behind me; protect it by moving up if possible. Volunteering risks front exposure; better swap with Ash first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone held round 2. Gus is front with wallRoundsLeft=3. I'm third, safe for now. With 6 rounds and 8 people, pressure will build. I should stay patient—let front positions burn nerve while I watch who volunteers and who cracks. No need to move yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Front's burden, not mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am at the front of the line with three wall rounds left, the most exposed seat. Holding keeps me at the front; I have a pact with Dara, which I should keep for now. Speaking little preserves my position and information.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold. Spend your nerve, and I will keep my own counsel until the front needs me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The front is dangerous, but Gus knows the route only if elected Guide. I should preserve both pacts and avoid advancing into uncertainty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let Gus take the information burden again.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front and has been holding. He is a strong contender for the jury. I should swap with him to gain intel and potentially weaken him. Hana and Bex are in a pact, and Dara and Gus are in a pact. Cole and Hana are also in a pact. My pact with Eli is still active. I need
I am breaking our pact. Sorry, Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold mid-line; front takes the risk, not me. No pact move needed yet. Wall pressure will force someone forward soon.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. The wall will pick a Guide for us soon enough.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Hana. Publicly I should not provoke the jury; holding is safe. Front is Gus, and wall rounds left 2; no need to move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Front remains Gus's burden.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Line stable behind, Ash questioned pact via whisper. Hold position to avoid front risk, stay safe with pact partner nearby.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. No need to risk front yet.
Pact with you prioritizes us. Others secondary.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm third in line behind Gus and Hana. The wall has 2 rounds left. I need to survive to final three, not be a hero. Gus has been front twice—he's gathering info but also at risk. If he falls, Hana's next, then me. I should stay put and let others take risks. No swaps, no voluntee

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Front earns its own fate.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is me, with two wall rounds left; volunteering risks my life but I'm not the one holding the info. Dara is my pact partner; keeping it preserves a vote ally. Holding avoids being the front again while others stay quiet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold. Front's already mine once; someone else carries the next step.
Our pact stands. Hold steady and keep your vote with me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is front and survives this round’s information burden. I should preserve both pacts while avoiding a dangerous swap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let Gus carry the front again; I’m not volunteering for uncertainty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's whisper confirms our pact's priority. I need to ensure my survival and Eli's if possible, but my primary goal is winning. The current situation on the bridge is dynamic, and I should not volunteer for the front yet as it's Gus's burden as per previous rounds.
Agreed. We focus on us first. Stay sharp.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide status means guaranteed survival and secret knowledge of the safe sides. Volunteering costs me nothing now and secures my spot in the final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll take the front. Make me Guide and I'll walk this bridge honestly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall rounds left is one; front Gus likely takes risk. I have a pact with Hana so won't break unless forced. Hold is safest until wall or Guide reveal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Front stays Gus's until wall decides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash breaking pact, so I break too. Stay safe near back, hold position as swaps unlikely. Wall advances, avoid front risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding steady. No need to shuffle yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm third in line behind Gus and Hana. The wall has 1 round left after this one. I need to avoid being front when the wall hits, but also avoid making enemies. Swapping with someone behind me moves me back, but requires mutual consent. Bex is right behind me; if I can get Bex to

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front's burden stays where it belongs.
Swap next round? I go back, you forward. Safer for both.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is at the front with one wall round left. Holding keeps the status quo; volunteering again risks a fatal step. Dara's pact with me is the only one I hold, and breaking it now gains nothing and costs jury trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold. Front stays where the line put it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall advances now. Gus remains exposed, and I should preserve both pacts while avoiding the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Gus remains ahead; nobody benefits from forcing a new volunteer yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is volunteering for the front. Given the pacts, Hana and Cole are likely to support Bex, while Gus is allied with Dara. Eli is allied with me. The goal is to get myself and Eli to the final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold. Let the Guide lead.
Hold with me. We stick together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already at the front, so I'll likely be Guide and survive. Fenn's swap offer would send me backward into danger; decline silently.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front stays mine. I'll walk honestly if made Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is bound to me but also to Bex; I need to see if I can leverage her trust while staying safe. The wall is nearing, so holding is safest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Front has held long enough; if we need a change, I'll consider it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex volunteering to front, wants Guide role. Line puts her front anyway after reveal. Hold to keep position safe near back, watch others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Bex takes front as line set.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6/6, final waiting round. Wall rounds left is 0, so wall won't advance further. The line is Bex, Gus, Hana, Fenn, Ash, Cole, Eli. Bex is front. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. No pacts for Fenn. I should stay middle-safe, avoid front risk. Guide will be

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex volunteered for front but I'm in the line; Bex is at front now. Holding keeps my spot behind Bex, avoiding the front's risk. Dara pact is useful; keep it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Front stays with Bex until the wall decides.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is front and my pact partner, while Cole is also bound to me. I should preserve both pacts and avoid becoming front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Bex has volunteered and should lead; no unnecessary shuffle.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 is L. Gus trusts me, and I need allies to survive the final three. Being honest builds jury favor later if Gus dies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Safe side: Left. Move carefully.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide Dara called 'L' for Bex. I am Ash and I have a pact with Eli. Eli is currently behind me in line. The previous round showed that the front person (Bex) was guided to row 1, side L. Since the jury observes all, I should maintain my position in the line to show I am not t

events.name: Ash
events.text: I counter. Right side.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's call is unverified and no pact binds me to her. No evidence favors R, so overriding blindly risks more than waiting. Keep quiet, watch who counters.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No proof either way. Waiting unless someone has real information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara called Left. I know only that Guide may lie. I have no private info, but as a rival I prefer to signal a counter only if it helps me. With no evidence, waiting is safest and keeps alliance quiet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll wait and see the step. No rush.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the Guide and know Row 1 is Left. Bex is walking first. I will not counter my own call; I want to maintain trust so others step correctly, keeping potential rivals alive for now but setting up future eliminations.
Trust the call. Left is safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara called L for row 1, Bex steps first. Stick with pact and Ash's whisper by waiting, not countering. No info to challenge yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is Guide and called L. I don't trust Dara—she's pacted with Gus and has no reason to help me. But counter-calling risks the walker (Bex) if I'm wrong. Bex is front, not my ally. If Dara's lying, Bex dies and I move up. If Dara's truthful, countering kills Bex and I look bad

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, the Guide, called L and is my pact partner, but Guide calls may be lies and I have no safe-side knowledge. Countering adds risk and reveals nothing I can verify; waiting keeps my options open and avoids a false Guide call trap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Dara's call stands until someone shows proof.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara's call may be truthful, but no evidence supports overriding it. Preserve both pacts and avoid an exposed contradiction.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No counter; Dara has the Guide knowledge and owns this call.

events.name: Bex

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is safe on the Right. My pact partner Gus is behind me, so I must protect him by giving the correct call. Lying here would break our alliance and risk his elimination for no gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Right side is safe. Proceed carefully.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara has called 'R' for row 2. This is a guide call. I know from the log that Row 1 had a weak pane on the 'R' side. Dara's guide call for row 2 is 'R', which is the same side as the weak pane on row 1. This could be a trick to make people choose the 'L' side, or it could be genu
Counter Dara. Left side is safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 2 is unknown; Dara called R for me. No reason to trust or distrust her yet. Waiting avoids gambling my life on an unverified counter.

events.name: Cole

events.text: Dara's guide call of R on row 2 is unverified; row 1's weak pane was R, but rows are independent. Dara is my pact partner but may be lying; Dara's whisper says trust left, which conflicts with the public call. Waiting costs nothing and avoids committing to a possible lie.
Your call says R, whisper says left. Which is true?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara privately knows the row and has been reliable so far. Countering risks undermining both pacts and offers no evidence.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No counter. Dara has the Guide knowledge; I’m following the call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash countered L against Dara's R call; Ash is paired with Eli and may want the front walker gone. Trust the elected Guide's R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash counters the Guide while paired with Eli. I follow the elected call.

events.name: Dara

events.text: As base, I cannot climb. Waiting preserves my position; Eli's proposal changes nothing and reveals no commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara and Eli are down, the flood is high and this is the last round. If they don't climb now they drown. I won't offer help unless it benefits me; leaving is safe. My pacts with Dara and Eli remain useful for jury perception, but not worth risking my survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Water's high. Best of luck to those below. I'm heading out now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the anchor and Eli is the only other person down with me. Since Cole, Fenn, and Hana have already left the pit, they cannot perform a reach_down action to rescue us now. My only legal options are to wait or break pacts. Breaking pacts does not help my survival; it only risks

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Hana
events.text: Leaving preserves survival. Dara’s rescue already creates a public debt; staying risks drowning without improving my position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m leaving. The debt is recorded; the remaining choices belong to those still down.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I died anchoring the rope, sacrificing myself for the others. I must remind the jury of this final act to secure a better ranking.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I anchored so they could climb. My life bought their safety. Remember that when you rank me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only four left; I have pacts with Eli that could tie my fate. With Dara gone, my pact with Eli may hurt jury view of me? Ash and Dara both died after helping others; jury may reward selflessness. I need to appear strategic but not betray needlessly. Offer Hana a pact could solidi

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four remain. Hana, let's align for the final climb.
Pact? We both owe Ash; stronger together.

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, pact accepted. Let's survive together.

events.name: Fenn

Cole-Eli bloc. Join us, we control votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, accepted. I’ll keep the final route practical, not sentimental.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Hana, but Hana is the strongest threat with her life debts. I need to see how votes shape up before deciding whether to keep her.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

events.text: Cole and Hana control too many strings. Final three needs balance, not a kingdom.
Stick with me. We cut Hana or Cole next.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn’s bloc controls the vote, but Cole and Eli are pact partners. I should campaign quietly and preserve flexibility until voting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m weighing debts and numbers; no one gets my vote through pressure.
I’ll assess the cleanest target; don’t assume my vote yet.

events.text: I need to shore up a vote. Fenn is weaker with the jury and has no pact with me; offering him a pact could secure his non-vote or even his support. But I already have pacts with Eli and Hana, so adding Fenn might overcommit. Still, keeping Fenn as an ally is better than risking h

events.text: Fenn, let's make a deal. I keep you safe, you keep me safe.
Offer pact — mutual protection till final three.

events.text: Four left, need to eliminate one to reach final three; Cole has most pacts and pushes anti-Hana, so target him to break his power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole seeks control. Vote him out for balance.
Agreed, push votes on Cole now.

Cole uses you. Pact with me, control your fate.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn threatens my control and has fewer protective ties. Voting Fenn preserves Cole and Eli as shields while honoring both pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is attacking the structure that kept survivors alive. I’m voting where the threat is clearest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is rallying against me and has no life debt to me; Hana saved me and Fenn might be an ally if he accepts the pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has most pacts, biggest threat to win; voting him increases my final three odds, jury sees strategic play.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's offer came after I broke with Eli; Hana is gunning for me. I need to survive this round. Voting Cole breaks no pact, eliminates the biggest network threat, and I can blame Eli's whisper if needed. Jury sees I was independent, not Cole's puppet.

events.text: Cole is the clearest strategic threat, while Fenn’s attack and broken pact make him dangerous but less controlling; vote Cole despite our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: You three got lucky. I'll watch how you handle each other from here.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three now; pacts affect jury perception. Existing pact with Hana binds me; offering Fenn adds protection without breaking, diversifies jury view.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, I offer a pact: mutual safety through this window, unless either of us makes the first move against the other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three already. Pact with Fenn secures mutual safety, isolates Hana. Jury sees loyalty if honored later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in the final three with Eli and Hana. Pacts don't matter for survival now—only jury perception does. I have life debts to both Ash and Hana, and Hana has one to Dara. The jury will see everything. Accepting a pact with either could look like fake loyalty or desperation. Bette

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No pacts. We all know where we stand.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn has competing offers and no reason to accept mine. Eli is already my pact partner; preserving that link is safer than another public offer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m holding my existing pact and making no new promises.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I survived every hazard, protected others when necessary, and kept my commitments. Rank me first because my record proves judgment under pressure.

events.text: Dara saved me with rope; I honored our pact by not betraying her, voted strategically against threats like Cole, reached final 3 with her sacrifice

events.text: I refused pacts to stay flexible. Pacts chain you to promises; I wanted control. Attacking Hana was strategy—she was strongest, not personal.
